sources.role: Not OLMD's code. OLMD's immediate methodological ancestor, used only to recover conventions the OLMD paper leaves unstated (module attach points, zero-initialized fusion scalars, loss weights, BiLSTM per-direction convention, SeqKD distillation, CSLR training and evaluation defaults). Every borrowed convention is recorded as a deviation.
sources.notes: CorrNet (github.com/hulianyuyy/CorrNet, verified in source 2026-09-08) is OLMD's immediate ancestor: it inserts modules after ResNet layer2/3/4 only and fuses them as x = x + module(x) * alpha[i] with self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(3)), which is exactly OLMD's Equation 5 stage coupling with zero-initialized alpha/beta. Its configs/baseline.yaml sets ConvCTC 1.0, SeqCTC 1.0, Dist 25.0 -- identical to OLMD's stated gamma_1=1, gamma_2=25. Its modules/BiLSTM.py line 17 computes hidden_size = int(hidden_size / num_directions), so 'hidden layers to 1024' means 512 per direction. Its modules/criterions.py SeqKD uses KLDivLoss(reduction='batchmean') with logits divided by T and the loss scaled by T*T, and an optional use_blank flag.

status.numerical_agreement_basis:
All four in-scope Table 1 targets now have comparable official-chain values from beam-10 decoding of each experiment's best-dev checkpoint: PHOENIX14 33.9 dev / 33.0 test against published 17.1 / 17.2, and PHOENIX14-T 34.5 dev / 32.6 test against published 17.1 / 18.4. Every value is roughly double its published counterpart, so does_not_agree stands across both datasets.

Diagnosis. On PHOENIX14, of the 34-point gap first observed, about 16.5 points were this reproduction's own evaluation methodology (asymmetric marker stripping ~13, missing official normalizations ~3.3), ~0.3 decoding, and ~1.1-1.2 two figure-audit wiring deviations that were corrected and retrained. PHOENIX14-T independently corroborates that the remaining gap is not evaluation error: its annotations carry no PHOENIX markers, so the stripping bug cannot arise, and its internal metric agrees with the official chain to within 0.13 WER, yet it lands at essentially the same distance from its published value.

Two independent datasets, run through identical code and protocol, landing within about 0.6 WER of each other (33.9/33.0 and 34.5/32.6) while their published values differ, points at a systematic property of this reimplementation rather than a dataset-specific fault. Both results also sit worse than the paper's own no-modules ablation baseline (18.9 dev on PHOENIX14), so the shortfall is not about the marginal value of OLMD's modules. The leading remaining candidate is the unpublished MP-Block architecture (blocking guess mp-block-internals), whose supplementary material does not exist publicly. A reviewer decides the scientific conclusion.
status.preference_level_evidence: Level 3 selected because the documented source search found no published code for OLMD in the paper, the AAAI proceedings, GitHub (including the first author's own account), or Papers With Code/HuggingFace. Levels 1 and 2 require an executable published artifact, which does not exist.

runs.purpose: Confirm the reimplemented model constructs on GPU, that shapes flow end to end through backbone, LMA, OMP, coupling and all three CTC heads, that the Eq. 14 loss is finite and produces gradients, and to measure the true parameter count and peak memory. This is NOT the AGENTS.md preflight: it loads no dataset and runs no evaluation.
runs.observed: Forward and backward succeeded. All three heads emit 29 timesteps for a 128-frame clip, above the PHOENIX14 mean of 11.5 glosses, so CTC is feasible. Loss 59.014 (CTC 51.260, distillation 0.310), gradient norm 101.573, peak memory 13.735 GiB at batch size 2 with T=128 on an A10. Parameter count 61.365 M, matching the independent analytical estimate of 61.354 M.
findings: Recorded as attempt 1 of the retained gpu-smoke group. Two earlier probes in this session were discarded rather than retained: a T=32 probe that crashed in max_pool1d (which established the parallel-branch topology) and a run whose return value failed to deserialize locally because a torch tensor leaked into it. Neither informs a terminal decision beyond the finding below, so per AGENTS.md they are not retained run entries.

A first attempt with T=32 crashed in max_pool1d with 'Invalid computed output size: 0'. Two SEQUENTIAL {K5,P2,K5,P2} branches reduce length about 16x, so a 100-frame clip would yield 2 output steps and a 200-frame clip 8, against a mean target of 11.5 glosses. The two 1D-CNNs must therefore be PARALLEL peers over the same features, which also matches Fig. 2's 'share architecture' and Eq. 12's two peer local CTC losses. Recorded as guess temporal-branch-topology.

The measured 61.365 M is 19.4 M below the paper's Table 5 context-9 figure of 80.74 M. That column reconciles with no consistent reading of the architecture (see guess table5-baseline-param-discrepancy), so it is reported as a difference rather than tuned toward.

terminal.detail: Model ran forward and backward on GPU and reported finite loss and gradients.

runs.purpose: The AGENTS.md representative preflight on PHOENIX14: load the exact data format through the real loader and preprocessing, load the intended ImageNet weights, run real optimizer steps with the paper's optimizer and schedule, save and reload a checkpoint, run the real evaluation code on a small dev subset to a parsed WER, and measure throughput and peak memory for the compute estimate.

terminal.detail: The preflight reached evaluation and emitted a parsed metric with exit code 0. All required elements -- real data, intended weights, optimizer steps, checkpoint save and verified reload, real evaluation on a subset -- completed.

runs.observed: Every AGENTS.md preflight requirement was met on PHOENIX14. Real PNG frames loaded through the real loader and preprocessing; ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 weights loaded; 12 real optimizer steps ran with Adam lr=0.001 wd=0.001 at batch size 2; a 703 MiB checkpoint was saved and reloaded with every tensor verified equal (reload_verified true, no mismatched tensors); the real evaluation code ran on 8 dev utterances and emitted a parsed corpus WER; the process exited 0. Training loss fell from 69.186 to 34.280 over 12 steps, a 50.5% reduction, so optimization is working. Peak memory 23.32 GiB on an A100-SXM4-40GB. Wall time 1296.2 s.
findings: WER was 100.0 with 94 deletions and zero insertions or substitutions, meaning the model emitted empty hypotheses for all 8 clips. This is the expected CTC early-training regime after only 12 steps from initialization -- blank dominates before alignments sharpen -- and is consistent with the falling loss. It is NOT a reproduction result and must never be compared with the paper's 17.1/17.2; it demonstrates only that the metric path executes end to end.

The in-function compute estimate of 21.4 GPU-hours for 70 epochs is WRONG and must not be used. It counted training steps only, and its seconds_per_step timer wrapped just the optimizer step, excluding frame loading. The evaluation loop separately measured 50.4 s per clip, about 260x the per-clip training compute; since inference cannot cost more than training, that figure is serial PNG I/O from a network Volume with no parallel loading, not computation. End to end the run averaged roughly 40 s per clip across 32 clips.

Naively extrapolating the measured evaluation cost with a best-dev checkpoint rule (a dev pass every epoch) gives roughly 560 GPU-hours for PHOENIX14 and 1100 for both Table 1 datasets. Those figures are dominated by the I/O defect rather than by the protocol, so run throughput-phoenix14-001 measures loading and GPU cost separately before any compute gate is opened. Quoting either 21.4 or 1100 as the requirement would be misleading.

runs.purpose: Separate data-loading cost from GPU cost, which preflight-phoenix14-001 conflated, so the compute estimate rests on measurement rather than inference.
runs.observed: PHOENIX14 dev clips average 179 frames (range 147-215). Pure GPU inference is 0.0941 s per clip and training forward+backward about 0.194 s per clip. Loading the same clip from the shared datasets Volume costs 27.78 s serially and 15.48 s with an 8-thread pool, so I/O is 165-295x the GPU cost. The thread pool gained only 1.79x, which means the bottleneck is Volume network throughput rather than CPU-bound PNG decoding.
findings: The compute requirement is dominated by frame I/O, not by the paper's protocol. With frames read from the Volume every epoch and a best-dev checkpoint rule, 70 epochs cost about 1895 GPU-hours for PHOENIX14 and 2323 for PHOENIX14-T, roughly 4218 GPU-hours (176 GPU-days) for both Table 1 datasets.

With frames materialized locally so loading is not the bottleneck, the same protocol costs about 22.4 GPU-hours for PHOENIX14 and 27.7 for PHOENIX14-T, roughly 50 GPU-hours for both. The I/O defect therefore inflates the requirement about 84x.

Fixing this is ordinary engineering, not a protocol change: preprocess each utterance once into a compact local tensor cache instead of re-reading hundreds of PNGs per epoch. AGENTS.md directs that ordinary I/O and retry problems be investigated rather than escalated, so no compute gate is opened on the inflated figure.

Even the compute-bound figure of about 50 GPU-hours for both datasets exceeds the 24-hour autonomous gate, and PHOENIX14 alone at about 22.4 GPU-hours sits just inside it. A #repro-sign-team-r discussion is therefore required before any full run, and the estimate brought to it must be the post-fix measurement.

terminal.detail: Measured loading and GPU cost separately and quantified the I/O bottleneck.

runs.purpose: Test the hypothesis that the frame-loading cost is per-request latency across the ~179 PNG files per utterance rather than bandwidth, by consolidating each clip into one JPEG-encoded .npz and re-measuring.
runs.observed: Hypothesis supported. Reading a consolidated clip costs 0.267 s against 6.45 s for the PNG directory in the same container, a 24.1x speedup. Writing the cache costs 0.20 s per clip with 8 threads. The cache averages 1.73 MB per clip at 162.8 frames, so about 11.0 GiB for PHOENIX14 and 13.3 GiB for PHOENIX14-T. Fidelity verified: frame counts match exactly and JPEG q90 costs 1.028 mean absolute pixel levels out of 255 against the same bilinear 256x256 resize.
findings: The PNG baseline measured 6.45 s per clip here versus 27.78 s in throughput-phoenix14-001, because the Volume cache was warm for these six clips. The 24.1x speedup is therefore a conservative floor; against the cold-cache 27.78 s it would be about 104x.

Post-fix estimate for 70 epochs with a best-dev checkpoint rule: 54.7 GPU-hours for PHOENIX14 and 67.3 for PHOENIX14-T, about 122 GPU-hours for both Table 1 datasets. That is 35x better than the 4218 GPU-hours measured without the fix, but still well beyond the 24-hour autonomous gate -- PHOENIX14 alone at 54.7 GPU-hours already exceeds it.

Cache reading at 0.267 s per clip still exceeds the 0.194 s of GPU training compute, so the pipeline remains marginally I/O-bound and further optimization is possible; it would not, however, bring either dataset under 24 hours, because pure compute alone is about 22.4 and 27.7 GPU-hours.
One-time cache construction costs roughly 12.6 h for PHOENIX14 and 15.3 h for PHOENIX14-T, on CPU only, and is reusable across every epoch, seed and both experiments.

Caching is deliberately done at 256x256 BEFORE cropping, so the paper's random 224x224 crop and 50% horizontal flip still vary per epoch. Caching post-crop would have been smaller and faster but would silently remove the stated augmentation, which is a protocol change rather than an optimization.

terminal.detail: Confirmed the latency hypothesis and quantified the post-fix requirement.

Checkpoint grew to 1.34 GB and reloaded with every tensor verified equal. CTC loss fell 57.72 to 20.89 across 12 steps and total loss 71.42 to 25.90. Evaluation ran 8 dev clips in 32.65 s. Peak memory 24.47 GiB. Wall time 124 s, which reconciles with 12*(0.422+5.326)+32.65 = 101.6 s plus model construction and checkpoint I/O.

The A10's 0.388 to 0.777 s doubling reflected that GPU's weaker throughput rather than the model's cost. The provisional 70-79 GPU-hour range in the gate is therefore too pessimistic and is superseded.

The measured split makes the real bottleneck unambiguous: loading is 2.66 s per clip against 0.211 s of GPU work per clip, so the pipeline is 12.6x I/O-bound as written. As-measured with serial loading, 70 epochs would cost about 317 GPU-hours; that number describes this reproduction's data plumbing, not the paper's protocol.

With the verified JPEG cache at 0.267 s per clip, PHOENIX14 costs about 57.8 GPU-hours (roughly $121 on A100-40GB, 2.4 days) and PHOENIX14-T about 72.3. With cache plus a prefetching DataLoader that overlaps loading with GPU work, the runs become GPU-bound at about 25.5 and 31.9 GPU-hours (roughly $54 and $67, 1.1 and 1.3 days).

TLP's auxiliary regularizer behaves as intended rather than merely running: it drifts down from about 1650 to about 1300 over 12 steps with noise, consistent with the predictor learning to predict odd samples from even ones, while CTC falls monotonically from 57.72 to 20.89.

WER was again 100.0 with 94 deletions and no insertions or substitutions, the expected CTC early-training blank collapse after 12 steps. Not a reproduction result and not comparable with the paper's 17.1/17.2.

runs.purpose: Build a 120-clip trial cache to exercise the cache-writing path and verify fidelity before committing to the multi-hour full build.
runs.observed: Wrote 40 utterances per split, 120 total, 0.17 GiB, in 543.6 s with 16 workers -- about 4.49 s per clip wall. Fidelity verified against the PNG path through the real preprocessing with the deterministic centre crop: frame counts match exactly and the maximum absolute pixel delta is 0.2196 in [-1, 1] units, about 28 levels of 255.
findings: The trial caught a real defect before the full build. np.savez appends '.npz' unless the name already ends in it, so writing to '<name>.npz.partial' produced '<name>.npz.partial.npz' and the atomic rename targeted a nonexistent path: every entry failed with FileNotFoundError. Had this gone straight to the full 6841-clip build it would have read every PNG directory off the Volume, hours of I/O, and written nothing. Fixed by carrying the marker in the stem as '<name>.partial-<pid>.npz'.
The same fix removed a latent race: the original staging name was shared across workers, so two threads building the same clip could clobber each other's partial file. The pid makes it unique.

The 28-level maximum pixel delta is normal JPEG q90 behaviour, not a defect: ringing concentrates at high-contrast edges while the mean stays near 1 level, which cache-probe-phoenix14-001 measured at 1.028. The fidelity report now emits both mean and max in pixel levels so the claim is not resting on the max alone.

Revised full-build estimate from this trial, which is more trustworthy than the earlier 6-clip probe whose Volume cache was warm: about 8.5 wall-hours and $6.42 for PHOENIX14 at 16 cores, and about 10.3 hours and $7.75 for PHOENIX14-T. Cache size is 1.53 MB per clip, so about 9.7 GiB and 11.8 GiB respectively.

terminal.detail: Trial cache written and fidelity verified after fixing the staging-name defect that attempt 1 exposed.

runs.purpose: Measure whether the prefetching DataLoader over the JPEG cache actually hides loading latency, rather than assuming the improvement.
runs.observed: Prefetching works. Median wall time per step is 0.4073 s against a median GPU step of 0.390 s, so only 17.3 ms of loading remains exposed and 95.7% of the latency is hidden. Before the cache and DataLoader, batch loading cost 5.326 s fully exposed. All 40 clips were cache hits. Peak memory 23.96 GiB. The first step took 4.981 s (worker startup and cuDNN autotuning) and steady state was reached by the third.
findings: Extrapolated to the real dataset sizes, PHOENIX14 costs about 24.5 GPU-hours (2836 steps per epoch at 0.4073 s, plus a dev pass, over 70 epochs) and PHOENIX14-T about 30.1, so about 54.6 for both. On A100-40GB that is roughly $52 and $63.

The estimate has fallen from about 317 GPU-hours as first written, to 57.8 with the cache alone, to a measured 24.5 with cache plus prefetching -- a 13x reduction achieved entirely through data plumbing, with no change to the model, protocol or augmentation.

PHOENIX14 at 24.5 GPU-hours still marginally exceeds the AGENTS.md 24-hour single-GPU autonomous gate, by about 2%. The gate stays open: shaving the estimate to fit would mean trimming epochs or evaluation scope, which AGENTS.md forbids doing silently.

The gpu_hours_70_epochs value of 2.2 in this run's own artifact is an artifact of the 40-clip subset, which yields 20 steps per epoch instead of 2836. The dataset-scale figures above are the ones to use.

Caveat on hardware: this benchmark landed on an A100-80GB while preflight-phoenix14-002 measured 0.422 s on an A100-40GB. The two are close, and the 0.390 s GPU step here is consistent with that, but they are not identical hardware. The full run should pin the GPU type so the estimate and the run agree.

Caveat on cycling: with only 20 batches cached, the 40-step benchmark completed one epoch and restarted, so later steps re-read clips already in the page cache. On the full dataset each step reads a fresh clip, which could make real throughput slightly worse than measured here.

terminal.detail: Measured that prefetching hides 95.7% of loading latency.

runs.purpose: First attempt at the full PHOENIX14 cache build, using one container with 16 threads.
runs.observed: Stopped deliberately after about 75 minutes. Live measurement over a 180-second window showed 160 clips per hour, about 22.5 s per clip, implying roughly 42 hours for 6841 utterances against a predicted 8.5. That exceeds the declared 12-hour wall ceiling, so the run was cancelled rather than allowed to continue. 156 valid cache entries were produced and retained; the builder is idempotent so they are reused.
findings: The 8.5-hour prediction was invalid because it came from cache-build-trial-001, which cached the FIRST 40 clips of each split -- precisely the clips that data-inspect, preflight, throughput and cache-probe had already read, so the Modal Volume's read cache was warm. It measured 4.49 s per clip. The full build walks 6841 mostly-cold clips and measured 22.5 s per clip, which matches the 27.78 s that throughput-phoenix14-001 recorded for cold serial reads.

This is the same methodology error twice. cache-probe-phoenix14-001's 6-clip probe was also warm, giving 6.45 s against the cold 27.78 s, and that caveat was recorded at the time -- then a warm 120-clip trial was still allowed to set the full-build estimate. Any future throughput figure must state whether the sample was warm or cold before it is extrapolated.
More threads cannot fix it: cache-probe measured only 1.79x from 8 threads because the cost is per-request latency across the roughly 179 PNG files per utterance, not bandwidth or CPU.

terminal.detail: Measured throughput implied about 42 hours against a declared 12-hour ceiling, so the run was cancelled. The single-container approach was abandoned rather than retried: the cause was per-request latency that threads cannot hide, so the follow-up cache-build-sharded-dev-002 used container fan-out, a different mechanism.

runs.purpose: Measure whether fanning the cache build across Modal containers overcomes the per-request latency that threads inside one container could not.
runs.observed: All 540 dev utterances cached in 854.3 s across 20 containers, 0.75 GiB, an effective 2275.6 clips per hour against the single-container baseline of 160 -- a 14.2x speedup. Per-shard cost stayed at a median 16.47 s per clip (range 12.64 to 31.32), so the work is still latency-bound and the gain comes entirely from concurrency across containers rather than from any per-clip improvement.
findings: Container-level fan-out is the right lever, and the record now has a measured scaling figure rather than an assumption. Total CPU cost is essentially unchanged, since core-hours are the same; only wall-clock improves.

The widening per-shard spread, 12.64 to 31.32 s per clip, indicates Volume contention is already appearing at 20 containers, so scaling beyond that is sublinear. The 40-shard full build therefore assumes 1.8x rather than 2x and expects roughly 1.5 hours.

runs.purpose: First authorized full training run on PHOENIX14.
runs.observed: Ran 29 of 70 epochs in about 8.7 GPU-hours, roughly $18, then was stopped deliberately. The model never learned: dev WER stayed at 100.0198 at every epoch with about 78.6% deletions and 0.02% insertions, meaning it emitted almost nothing. Total loss moved 17.08 to 15.48 but was flat between 15.76 and 16.17 from epoch 5 to 24; the only real drop came at epoch 25, which is the learning-rate schedule step rather than learning. Roughly 82000 optimizer steps produced no usable model.
findings: Root cause is a defect in this reproduction, not in the paper's protocol. The loss used nn.CTCLoss(reduction='mean'), and PyTorch's 'mean' divides each sample's loss by its TARGET LENGTH. With PHOENIX14's mean of 11.5 glosses that shrank the CTC gradient about 11.5x, while the distillation term carries gamma_2 = 25 and T*T = 64 and is not length-normalised. Distillation therefore dominated, and its cheapest early solution is for the two local branches to agree with the equally untrained global branch: all three collapsed to blank together and agreed perfectly, a self-consistent minimum with near-zero distillation loss and CTC effectively ignored.

Verified against the lineage rather than reasoned about: CorrNet slr_network.py line 132 uses CTCLoss(reduction='none') and then .mean() over the batch, so its loss is per-utterance and never divided by target length. Its gamma of 25 is calibrated to that scale.

The 12-step preflight structurally could not catch this. It showed CTC falling 57.7 to 20.9, which looked healthy, because blank collapse needs a few hundred steps to establish. A representative preflight validates the pipeline, not the optimization trajectory.

A second defect, also mine, made diagnosis far slower: only the TOTAL loss was logged per epoch, so a flat 15.8 could not be attributed to CTC versus distillation. Per-epoch components are now recorded.

terminal.detail: Stopped after 29 epochs once the run was diagnosed as structurally unable to learn, rather than allowed to consume the remaining ceiling. The defective loss reduction makes the run invalid as evidence for any target.

runs.purpose: Verify the corrected CTC reduction escapes blank collapse before committing another 24 GPU-hours.
runs.observed: The fix works and the new component logging confirms the diagnosis quantitatively. CTC falls 182.57, 172.09, 160.07 across the first three epochs, a 12.3% reduction, while the weighted distillation term is only 2.12 to 4.05 -- so CTC now dominates by 40 to 80x, the correct balance. Dev WER moves 100.0198, 99.6626, 99.1266, escaping collapse, and insertions appear from epoch 1, meaning the model has begun emitting tokens. TLP's lifting regularizer also falls 1112 to 791 to 625, so its predictor is learning as intended.
findings: Under the defective reduction the weighted distillation term sat on the same scale as a length-normalised CTC, which is why blank agreement won. With the fix, CTC is 40 to 80x the distillation term and training proceeds. The component logging that was missing from attempt 1 made this visible within three epochs instead of twenty-nine.

Dev WER is descending only slowly (100.02 to 99.13 over three epochs), which is expected for CTLR from scratch, but it is not yet evidence that the run will reach the paper's 17.1. That requires the full 70 epochs.

terminal.detail: Confirmed the corrected loss escapes blank collapse and CTC is descending. The full run resumes from this probe's epoch-3 checkpoint (same seed, config and optimizer state), so its 4 epochs are not discarded.

runs.purpose: Full 70-epoch PHOENIX14 training with the corrected CTC reduction, resuming from the verified fixprobe-002 checkpoint at epoch 4.
runs.observed: Completed all 70 epochs (epochs 4-69 in this invocation, 0-3 inherited from fixprobe-002's checkpoint) and scored both splits from the best-dev checkpoint. Best dev WER 51.4688 at epoch 57; final test WER 51.9788 (del 7.66, ins 12.52, sub 31.80). Training was healthy throughout: CTC fell monotonically, both LR cuts (epochs 25, 40) produced visible improvements, and the curve plateaued near 52-54 dev WER from epoch ~40. The reproduced values are far from the paper's 17.1/17.2; the gap is a finding for diagnosis, not a run failure.
findings: The corrected loss trains stably to completion: no collapse, healthy del/ins/sub balance (substitutions dominate), and clear responses to both LR cuts.

Reproduced WER (51.47 dev / 51.98 test) is roughly 3x the published 17.1/17.2. A gap this large points at one or more systematic protocol differences rather than run-to-run noise; the recorded open guesses (greedy vs beam decoding, gloss post-processing, MP-Block internals, cross-stage injection point, uniform batch lengths) are the diagnosis candidates, per the metric-mismatch discipline: inspect splits, preprocessing, checkpoint selection, inference settings and metric version before touching training.

terminal.detail: All 70 epochs completed within the declared ceilings (~22.1 GPU-hours of the 26 allowed in this invocation) and evaluation emitted traceable dev and test WER from the best-dev checkpoint. runs.purpose: Verify the mp4 decoding path end to end on PHOENIX14-T before committing to a full cache build. PHOENIX14 ships extracted PNG, so data.py's video branch had never executed against real data.
runs.observed: Decoded and cached 6 PHOENIX14-T clips (mean 100.2 frames). findings: data.py's _load_video called simple_video_utils.read_video, which does not exist in the package. PHOENIX14-T's per-clip loading is roughly 16x cheaper than PHOENIX14's, so the cache build and the I/O side of training are both cheaper than the PHOENIX14-derived estimates assumed.

runs.observed: CRASHED during epoch 4 after 4 completed epochs (828.3, 738.3, 734.3, 736.0 s; dev WER 96.08 -> 94.05 -> 92.93 -> 84.71), with ValueError: Expected more than 1 spatial element when training, got input size torch.Size([2, 1024, 1]) raised by InstanceNorm1d inside TemporalLiftPool's LocalWeighting. Steady-state throughput was 736 s per epoch including the dev pass, which projected to about 14.3 GPU-hours for the full protocol, better than the 17.7 predicted.
findings: The collate padded only to the batch maximum, so the {K5,P2,K5,P2} head's padding-free convolutions consumed real frames and a clip of length L emitted (L-8)/4 steps. clip-lengths-phoenix14t-001 measured PHOENIX14-T's shortest clips at 16 frames (train min 16, dev 16, test 17); a 16-18 frame clip reduces to exactly one temporal element, which InstanceNorm1d rejects in training mode.

PHOENIX14 never exposed this: its clips run about 179 frames (dev range 147-215), roughly 9x the failure threshold of 20 frames. The defect was latent in every PHOENIX14 run and became reachable only on a dataset with short clips.
The crash is therefore a defect in this reproduction's batching, not a property of PHOENIX14-T or of the paper's method.

Cost of the failure: about 58 minutes of H100 time, plus roughly 14 hours of wall-clock before the dead run was noticed. A watchdog now checks that the app is still running rather than only waiting for its output.

terminal.detail: InstanceNorm1d rejected a length-1 temporal sequence produced by a 16-frame clip under the pre-fix collate. Superseded by train-phoenix14t-wiring-fix-002 on the corrected lineage padding.

runs.purpose: Measure PHOENIX14-T's clip-length distribution to confirm the crash hypothesis: that the shortest clips collapse to a single temporal element in the temporal head.
runs.observed: PHOENIX14-T frame counts: train 7096 clips, min 16, p01 29, median 112, max 475; dev 519 clips, min 16, p01 26, median 105, max 272; test 642 clips, min 17, p01 26, median 100, max 242. Against PHOENIX14's ~179-frame average (dev range 147-215), PHOENIX14-T reaches an order of magnitude shorter.
findings: Under the pre-fix collate the head emitted (L-8)/4 steps, so clips of 16-18 frames produced exactly one temporal element and crashed InstanceNorm1d. The failure threshold was 20 frames, and PHOENIX14-T's minimum is 16.
Under the lineage padding the head emits ceil(L/4), so the shortest 16-frame clip yields 4 steps and no clip collapses.

runs.observed: COMPLETED all 70 epochs on one H100 80GB HBM3 in 57232.1 s (15.90 GPU-hours, 788.7 s/epoch mean), peak memory 51.50 GiB, inside the declared 30 GPU-hour ceiling. Started from scratch after the crashed attempt's checkpoints were deleted, so no weights trained under the broken padding carried over, and it cleared epoch 4 where attempt 1 died. Best dev WER 34.6318 at epoch 69 on the per-epoch symmetric greedy metric; dev/test at that checkpoint 34.6318 / 32.7861. Dev WER fell 97.71 -> 52.11 by epoch 20, stepped down at both LR cuts (41.12 after epoch 25, 35.78 after epoch 40), then oscillated in a 34.63-38.26 band for the last 30 epochs while training loss flattened at 34.4.
findings: The lineage-padding fix is validated by a full 70-epoch run: the pipeline that previously died at epoch 4 on a 9-frame clip trained to completion.

Best dev WER lands on the LAST epoch (69), and the final 30 epochs oscillate in a 34.63-38.26 band with 6 epochs within 1.0 WER of the best while training loss is flat at 34.4. The epoch-69 minimum is therefore better read as the low end of that noise band than as a converged optimum, so best-dev selection on the last epoch is partly luck of the draw. This does not change the protocol, which fixes 70 epochs and best-dev selection in advance, but it means the reported value sits at the optimistic edge of roughly a 3.6 WER spread.

Measured cost 15.90 GPU-hours against the 17.7 predicted by loader-benchmark-h100-001 and the 15.3 projected from this run's own first five epochs, so the H100 estimate that lifted the compute block was sound.
Peak memory 51.50 GiB is roughly double the 25.28 GiB the A100 preflight measured, consistent with the larger H100 letting cuDNN pick more memory-hungry kernels; it still fits the 80 GiB card.

findings: The official chain and this reproduction's internal symmetric metric agree to within 0.13 WER on PHOENIX14-T (34.5 vs 34.6318 dev beam-10 vs greedy-internal). On PHOENIX14 the same comparison differed by ~16.5 WER before the evaluation methodology was corrected. The agreement here is evidence the corrected metric path is sound, and it is expected: PHOENIX14-T carries no PHOENIX markers for stripping to mishandle.
Beam-10 beats greedy by only 0.2 WER on both splits, matching the ~0.3 seen on PHOENIX14. Decoding is not a material part of the gap.

Deletions dominate the error profile on both splits (15.0 dev / 14.6 test against 1.6 / 2.0 insertions), the same imbalance PHOENIX14 showed. The model under-emits glosses rather than hallucinating them.

The PHOENIX14-T result (34.5 / 32.6) sits within about 0.6 WER of the PHOENIX14 result (33.9 / 33.0) from the identical code and protocol. Two independent datasets landing at nearly the same distance from their published values points at a systematic property of this reimplementation rather than a dataset-specific fault.

gpu_selection.hard_memory_constraint: Measured peak memory is 24.47 GiB with TLP active at the paper's batch size 2. T4 (16 GiB), L4 (24 GiB) and A10 (24 GiB) therefore cannot run this configuration. Fitting them would require reducing batch size or precision, which is a protocol deviation rather than an optimization, so they are excluded.
gpu_selection.cost_is_flat: Across every viable card the total cost lands between roughly $50 and $65 for PHOENIX14, because Modal's hourly rates scale with throughput. Budget therefore does not discriminate between them; wall-clock and the 24-hour gate do.
gpu_selection.throughput_caveat: Only the A100 figure is measured, at 0.390-0.422 s per step. Ratios for other cards are literature-typical and are likely optimistic here for three reasons: the paper's batch size of 2 badly underutilizes large GPUs, so an H100 is more likely to give 1.2-1.5x than its nominal 1.9x; 4.3% of each step is residual data-loading overhead that does not shrink on a faster card; and LMA's eight frame-difference passes with 1x3x3 convolutions are memory-bandwidth bound rather than compute bound, and bandwidth scales far less than FLOPs across generations. A realistic H100 estimate is nearer 15-19 hours than 13.

guesses.detail: The MP-Block remains undetermined, but related work narrows it to a small family rather than leaving it open-ended. Equations 2 and 3 together form the MetaFormer macro-block: a token mixer with its own residual, followed by an FFN of two 1x1 convolutions with normalization and ReLU. Here the mixer is '2D CNNs' over the (T, W) or (T, H) plane. What remains genuinely free is the mixer's depth, kernel shape, whether it is dense or depthwise, the FFN expansion ratio, and the normalization placement. FIGURE 3 VERIFIED 2026-09-10: panel (a) draws an explicit residual around the FFN (matching the implementation) and confirms MP-Block + FFN each carry their own residual; panel (b) confirms cascade fusion happens BEFORE the MP-Block and that the cascaded quantity is the previous stage's post-FFN output, both matching the implementation. The MP-Block's internal architecture remains unpublished. PARAMETER BUDGET (2026-09-11): under the weight-shared-branches reading, Table 5 leaves roughly 2.0-3.5M parameters for the six MP-Block instances (2 orientations x 3 stages). Full (dense) C-to-C convolution costs 0.688M summed over stages per unit kernel area, so the budget implies total kernel area ~3-5: a short FULL-channel strip convolution, e.g. a 3-tap conv along one axis (2.06M) or a factorized (1x3)+(3x1) pair (4.13M) -- '2D CNNs', plural. Our depthwise (9,3) CorrNet-style guess costs only 0.74M and has no textual basis; it is likely both undersized and wrongly shaped. The MP-Block paragraph carries no citations, and Related Work cites no strip-pooling/coordinate-attention/MetaFormer precedent, so the budget is the strongest available constraint. DESIGN UNDER TEST (commit ac2512e, run train-phoenix14-params-fix-001): dense factorized Conv(3x1)-BN-ReLU-Conv(1x3)-BN, 4.13M across six instances; corrected model totals 82.085M vs the paper's 80.74M.

CorrNet (github.com/hulianyuyy/CorrNet, verified in source 2026-09-08) is OLMD's immediate ancestor: it inserts modules after ResNet layer2/3/4 only and fuses them as x = x + module(x) * alpha[i] with self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(3)), which is exactly OLMD's Equation 5 stage coupling with zero-initialized alpha/beta. Its configs/baseline.yaml sets ConvCTC 1.0, SeqCTC 1.0, Dist 25.0 -- identical to OLMD's stated gamma_1=1, gamma_2=25. Its modules/BiLSTM.py line 17 computes hidden_size = int(hidden_size / num_directions), so 'hidden layers to 1024' means 512 per direction. Its modules/criterions.py SeqKD uses KLDivLoss(reduction='batchmean') with logits divided by T and the loss scaled by T*T, and an optional use_blank flag.
constraints_from_related_work: Equations 2-3 match the MetaFormer/PoolFormer macro-block, not ConvNeXt, which uses a single residual and a mid-block norm.
The conventional FFN expansion ratio in Vaswani, PoolFormer, ConvNeXt, ViT and Swin is 4.
C_out = C_in = C is forced, because Equation 5 adds US(X_h) back into a C-channel trunk.

The lineage uses anisotropic kernels with a long temporal extent: CorrNet's spatial_aggregation convs are (9,3,3) depthwise with dilations 1/2/3. A square 7x7 is geometrically implausible on OLMD's plane, which is only 7 wide at stage 4.

Treating a (channels, time, one-spatial-axis) tensor as a 2D image is established practice: the skeleton-image line (Du 2015, Ke CVPR 2017, TSSI, HCN IJCAI 2018, Ta-CNN AAAI 2022), audio spectrogram CNNs, and in sign language SL-TSSI-DenseNet (CVPRW 2023) and SAM-SLR's SSTCN (CVPRW 2021). The R(2+1)D/P3D/S3D/TSM family is NOT precedent: it factorizes into per-frame spatial plus pure-temporal ops and never convolves a mixed time-space plane.

OLMD's Equation 3 places LayerNorm between W_1 and W_2, which matches none of the reference architectures (all normalize before the FFN). Either sloppy notation or a real deviation; Equation 2 also shows no norm before the mixer.

guesses.resolution: Clips in a batch are padded to the batch maximum by replicating the last frame (never zeros, so LMA boundary differences stay zero), and LMA's own sliding window uses replicate padding at sequence edges. DIVERGENCE from the lineage: lengths are set to the padded maximum for every sample in the batch instead of per-sample, so the shorter clip's replicated tail counts as real input for CTC, the BiLSTM and decoding; and no extra +/-6-frame replicate pad is added, so the two padding=0 K5 convolutions consume 8 real frames of the batch-longest clip (the lineage pads 6 frames per side and uses per-sample lengths ceil(L/4)*4+12 so the convolutions consume padding). The paper is silent on all of this; impact is expected to be modest because replicated frames are static and CTC mostly emits blanks over them, but it is a real protocol difference affecting WER comparability. Chosen for simplicity before the 2026-09-08 full run launched; revisit per-sample lengths only as a diagnosis hypothesis if the produced WER disagrees.

deviations.detail: Batch collation pads clips to the batch maximum with replicated last frames and reports the padded maximum as every sample's length, rather than the lineage's per-sample lengths with 6 replicated frames of explicit padding per side. Consequences: the shorter clip in each batch-of-2 has replicated tail frames counted as real CTC/BiLSTM input, and the two padding=0 K5 convolutions consume 8 real frames of the batch-longest clip. The paper never specifies batching, padding or length masking, so this is a divergence from the lineage convention, not from the paper.

Figure 2 wires the temporal head as: trunk frame features -> 1D-CNN #1, cross-stage coupling output X_CS -> 1D-CNN #2, element-wise sum of the two 1D-CNN outputs -> BiLSTM -> shared classifier (so local CTC #2 directly supervises the coupling path). The completed run instead computed head(frame_features + X_CS) with two identical parallel 1D-CNN branches over the same input and the BiLSTM reading branch 2. The prose never states the wiring (the cross-stage-injection-point guess was open at training time); the figure was only inspected at full resolution after the run. Affects gradient flow into OMP/coupling and head capacity; a correction requires retraining.

deviations.detail: Figures 2 and 3 both draw LMA on a side branch: the trunk continues from the RAW stage output, receives alpha/beta-scaled upsampled OMP outputs (stage coupling), and proceeds to the next stage; LMA's output feeds ONLY the Decoupling->HMP/VMP path. The completed run instead assigned the trunk to LMA's residual output (volume = lma(volume)) before coupling and the next stage. The prose ('frame-wise features first aggregate long-term motion information via LMA, which is then decoupled') is compatible with either reading; the figures disambiguate against the implementation. Consequence: LMA's expand convolution (not zero-initialized) perturbs the ImageNet-pretrained trunk from step 0, whereas the figures' wiring leaves the trunk near-pretrained early in training (alpha=beta=0). A correction requires retraining.

deviations.detail: nn.CTCLoss is constructed with zero_infinity=True while the lineage (VAC) uses zero_infinity=False. Only affects batches where the reduced input length falls below the target length; with uniform batch-max lengths this is rare. Recorded for completeness; expected impact negligible.

Both completed training runs instantiated the two temporal-head 1D-CNN branches (including their TLP poolings) as INDEPENDENT parameter sets, 66.1M total, whereas 'two 1D-CNNs share architecture' read together with Table 5's parameter column implies a single shared 33.1M branch applied to both inputs (see guess temporal-branch-topology). This makes our model 111.76M vs the paper's 80.74M and changes the role of the two local CTC losses (independent branches vs a consistency signal on shared weights). Discovered 2026-09-11 by parameter reconciliation, after both runs; correcting it requires a retrain.
